parts.label: (a)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
$X\in\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}$, with at least one valid probability $0<P(X=x)<1$. [B1]
Guidance: Correct distinct $X$ values and at least one linked probability strictly between 0 and 1; additional zero-probability values are allowed, but repeated $X$ values are not.
$P(X=-2)=\frac1{16},\ P(X=-1)=\frac3{16},\ P(X=0)=\frac5{16}$. [B1]
Guidance: Three correct probabilities linked to correct outcomes; a table is not required.
$P(X=1)=\frac5{16},\ P(X=2)=\frac2{16}$, so the distribution is $\left(\frac1{16},\frac3{16},\frac5{16},\frac5{16},\frac2{16}\right)$. [B1]
Guidance: The remaining two probabilities linked correctly. If fewer than three probabilities are correct, special-case B1 is available for four to six distinct values whose probabilities sum to 1 within 0.01.
Total: 3

parts.label: (b)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
$\operatorname{Var}(X)=\frac1{16}(-2)^2+\frac3{16}(-1)^2+\frac5{16}(0)^2+\frac5{16}(1)^2+\frac2{16}(2)^2-(0.25)^2$. [M1]
Guidance: Use $E(X^2)-[E(X)]^2$ with $(0.25)^2$. Follow through a table containing at least three distinct $X$ values and probabilities strictly between 0 and 1; allow one probability error if all remain below 1.
$\operatorname{Var}(X)=\frac54-\frac1{16}=\frac{19}{16}=1.1875$. [A1]
Guidance: Accept $1.188$ or $1.19$ only when reached without wrong working.
Total: 2
